facts.subject: Burg of the Four Friths
facts.statement: No castle; the burghers say the whole Burg is a castle.

refs.q: the whole Burg, houses and all, was a castle

facts.subject: Burg of the Four Friths
facts.statement: Houses stout, plain, neither poor nor lordly; folk dark and low, plainly but stoutly clad.

refs.q: he saw no poor or wretched houses, and none very big as of great lords

facts.subject: Burg of the Four Friths
facts.statement: Most men carry weapons and staves and wear short brown or blue jerkins, ready for battle.

refs.q: The more part of the men wore weapons at their sides and had staves in hand

refs.q: foot-men, with bills some, and some with bows, and all-armed knights and sergeants a-horseback

facts.subject: (unnamed) host of the Burg

ledger.summary: Ralph walks the Burg alone. Its folk are dark, short and plainly but stoutly dressed; tall fair women in short yellow embroidered gowns with an iron ring on the right arm are thralls. Merchants in long gowns and turbans trade in booths. At the South Gate the Burg's host returns with wounded men, cattle, sheep, horses, spoil and women captives only. A carline sings a raiding song. A yellow-gowned damsel takes offence at his question about the captives, and the carline curses her as a thrall. Ralph longs to see the Lady of the Wildwood again.
ledger.geography_notes: The Burg has a North and a South Gate facing each other, an East Gate, a wide clear way inside the wall, and wide ways running from the Great Place to each gate. There is no castle: the burghers say the whole Burg is a castle. There is a fish and fowl market. A narrow street runs east from the South Gate.
